title: Week in Orbit
summary: This week, the space industry is buzzing with contracts, launches, and a few delays. As the Space Force invests heavily in satellite capabilities, commercial players are also making strides in both space and defense sectors.

themes.title: Government Contracts Galore
themes.body: Northrop Grumman's $398 million satellite contract from the Space Force underscores the ongoing push for enhanced military space capabilities. Meanwhile, Palantir's $480 million extension on the TITAN ground station program signals a robust appetite for data integration in defense.

themes.title: Commercial Launches Continue
themes.body: SpaceX's CRS-34 mission to the ISS reinforces its dominance in cargo delivery, while Virgin Galactic is still trying to convince us that commercial space tourism is just around the corner. The real question remains: will the market be ready for these services when they finally arrive?

themes.title: International Collaborations on the Rise
themes.body: The upcoming ESA-China SMILE mission highlights an increasing trend of international partnerships in space exploration. Such collaborations may become essential as nations navigate the complexities of space governance and shared scientific goals.

themes.title: Emerging Players and Innovations
themes.body: True Anomaly's $190 million Series C round reflects the growing interest in space domain awareness, while Anduril and L3Harris's tactical SDA constellation bid showcases the melding of defense tech with space capabilities. As new players enter the field, the competitive landscape is set to shift.
